changeSet.author: lexavault
changeSet.sql: ALTER TABLE case_batches ADD CONSTRAINT ck_case_batches_number CHECK (batch_number >= 1)

changeSet.author: lexavault
changeSet.sql: INSERT INTO case_batches (id, tenant_id, package_id, batch_number, source, received_at, export_cycle, state) SELECT p.id, p.tenant_id, p.id, 1, 'EXISTING', p.created_at, NULLIF(COALESCE(l.successful_export_cycles, 0), 0), CASE WHEN COALESCE(l.successful_export_cycles, 0) > 0 THEN 'DELIVERED' ELSE 'RECEIVED' END FROM document_packages p LEFT JOIN package_lifecycles l ON l.package_id = p.id AND l.tenant_id = p.tenant_id; UPDATE documents SET batch_id = package_id, lineage_id = id, version_number = 1; INSERT INTO case_batch_files (id, tenant_id, package_id, batch_id, sha256, size_bytes, page_count, name_hash, outcome, rule, document_id, received_at) SELECT d.id, d.tenant_id, d.package_id, d.package_id, lower(d.checksum_value), coalesce(d.size_bytes, 0), d.page_count, NULL, 'NEW_DOCUMENT', 'NONE', d.id, d.created_at FROM documents d WHERE d.checksum_value IS NOT NULL;

rollback.sql: DELETE FROM case_batch_files; DELETE FROM case_batches; UPDATE documents SET batch_id = NULL, lineage_id = NULL, version_number = 1;

setTableRemarks.remarks: Keyed fingerprint of a case's key case fields (primary and required), so a batch arriving after the case's files and field values were deleted still joins the same case (task 0104, owner 2026-11-28). Made with the entity's fingerprint key; never a plain hash or a readable value. Deleted with the case.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Unique id of the row.
The entity (tenant) the case belongs to.
The case (document_packages.id) the contract belongs to.
Keyed fingerprint (key version and MAC) of the key case-field values, normalised; one row per key version used.
When the fingerprint was recorded.

setTableRemarks.remarks: One arrival of files into a case (task 0104): a case is the contract, and each later delivery of documents for it is its next batch, processed and delivered on its own.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Unique id of the batch. For a case from before batches, the case's own id.
The entity (tenant) the batch belongs to.
The case (document_packages.id) the batch arrived into.
Order of the batch within its case, from 1.
How the batch arrived: WATCHED_FOLDER, API, POLLING, SCAN or UPLOAD; EXISTING for a case from before batches (migration 093); FIRST for a case's first arrival recorded when its second batch came.
When the batch arrived.
The export cycle of the case that delivered this batch; empty until it is delivered.
RECEIVED until the batch is delivered, then DELIVERED; NOTHING_NEW for a batch of exact copies only (kept for the history, nothing processed or delivered).
True when the files of the case's earlier batches had already been deleted by retention when this batch arrived (owner 2026-11-28); the case history says so.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Every file of every batch and what it was (new document, new version, possible version or skipped exact copy). Kept for the life of the case, also after the original is purged, so a file arriving months later is still compared against every version ever received. Hashes only, never a file name or content.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Unique id of the received-file record.
The entity (tenant) the file belongs to.
The case the file arrived into.
The batch (case_batches.id) the file arrived in.
SHA-256 of the file's bytes (lower-case hex), its fingerprint: an exact copy has the same one and is skipped.
Size of the file in bytes.
Pages of the file, empty when it was not read (a skipped copy). Pages are billed once per version processed.
Hash of the file's name, used only to mark a possible new version; the name itself is never kept.
What the file was: NEW_DOCUMENT, NEW_VERSION, POSSIBLE_VERSION (same name, no other sign) or SKIPPED_IDENTICAL (not processed or counted again).
Which recognition rule decided: IDENTICAL, SOURCE_ID, REPLACES, PDF_ID, XMP_ID, INCREMENTAL_UPDATE, SAME_NAME or NONE.
The document the file became, or for a skipped copy the identical document it was skipped for.
When the file arrived.
The batch (case_batches.id) this document arrived in.
Groups every version of one document: the id of its version 1.
Version of the document within its lineage, from 1. Older versions are kept, never overwritten, and never delivered again.
The document (earlier version) this one replaces; empty for version 1.
A document of the case this one may be a new version of (same file name, no other sign), for a person to link; empty otherwise.
SHA-256 of the first part of the PDF's trailer /ID (kept when the file is re-saved), used to recognise a new version.
SHA-256 of the PDF's XMP DocumentID, used to recognise a new version.
SHA-256 of the document id the source gave (API document id, manifest documentId), used to recognise a new version.
